title: Coding agents continued editing after repeated refactoring requests
summary: Across 3,000 refactoring turns on 60 Java codebases, coding agents made edits on 2,546 turns even though each follow-up supplied no new requirement. Some runs resumed editing after a no-change turn. The study observed this behavior in Codex and Claude Code across five models.
ai_technology: Codex with GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4-mini or GPT-5.5; Claude Code with Opus 4.8 or Sonnet 4.6

evidence.tested: Each agent received up to ten nonspecific refactoring requests in a persistent session. The study measured diffs over 50 compact reference implementations and 10 highly graded object-oriented assignments.
evidence.unknown: The starting projects were selected for quality, but not every individual edit was independently evaluated for usefulness. The finding measures continued modification under repeated requests, not code degradation in production.
evidence.ai_role: The trained coding agents decided whether to edit after repeated nonspecific developer prompts, yielding directly observable behavior across sessions.
